title: Entra guest user report with stale invitations and last sign-in
summary: Microsoft Graph PowerShell script that exports every B2B guest with invitation state, age, last sign-in and optional group count, and flags stale invitations and inactive guests.
body:
# Entra guest user report with stale invitations and last sign-in

Guests accumulate quietly: project partners, vendors, one-off invitations. This script gives you a reviewable CSV of all guest accounts in Microsoft Entra ID, with the signals you need to decide who stays.

## What it does
- Reads all users with userType Guest through Microsoft Graph.
- Adds invitation state (PendingAcceptance or Accepted), account age, external domain and last sign-in.
- Optionally counts group memberships per guest (slower, one call per guest).
- Classifies each guest as Active, InactiveGuest or StaleInvitation based on a threshold you set.
- Exports a CSV and prints a per-domain summary.

## Script
```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Exports a report of Entra ID guest users.
.EXAMPLE
  .\Get-GuestReport.ps1 -StaleDays 120 -IncludeGroupCount
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string]$OutputPath = ".\GuestUserReport_$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd').csv",
    [ValidateRange(1,3650)]
    [int]$StaleDays = 90,
    [switch]$IncludeGroupCount
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# 1. Connect with read-only delegated scopes (no secrets in the script)
try {
    Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.Read.All','AuditLog.Read.All' -NoWelcome
}
catch {
    Write-Error "Connection to Microsoft Graph failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    return
}

# 2. Read all guests, selecting only the properties we need
$props = 'id','displayName','mail','userPrincipalName','companyName','createdDateTime',
         'externalUserState','externalUserStateChangeDateTime','accountEnabled','signInActivity'
try {
    $guests = Get-MgUser -Filter "userType eq 'Guest'" -All -Property $props -PageSize 500
}
catch {
    Write-Error "Could not read guest users: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    return
}
Write-Host "Found $($guests.Count) guest accounts." -ForegroundColor Cyan

$cutoff = (Get-Date).AddDays(-$StaleDays)
$report = foreach ($g in $guests) {
    $sa = $g.SignInActivity
    $lastSignIn = @($sa.LastSuccessfulSignInDateTime, $sa.LastSignInDateTime, $sa.LastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime) |
        Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Descending | Select-Object -First 1

    $groupCount = $null
    if ($IncludeGroupCount) {
        try { $groupCount = @(Get-MgUserMemberOf -UserId $g.Id -All -ErrorAction Stop).Count }
        catch { $groupCount = -1 }   # -1 = lookup failed
    }

    $status = 'Active'
    if ($g.ExternalUserState -eq 'PendingAcceptance' -and $g.CreatedDateTime -lt $cutoff) {
        $status = 'StaleInvitation'
    }
    elseif ($g.ExternalUserState -ne 'PendingAcceptance' -and (-not $lastSignIn -or $lastSignIn -lt $cutoff)) {
        $status = 'InactiveGuest'
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        DisplayName     = $g.DisplayName
        Mail            = $g.Mail
        Domain          = if ($g.Mail) { ($g.Mail -split '@')[-1] } else { '' }
        Company         = $g.CompanyName
        AccountEnabled  = $g.AccountEnabled
        InvitationState = $g.ExternalUserState
        Created         = $g.CreatedDateTime
        AgeDays         = [int]((Get-Date) - $g.CreatedDateTime).TotalDays
        LastSignIn      = $lastSignIn
        GroupCount      = $groupCount
        Status          = $status
        ObjectId        = $g.Id
    }
}

$report | Sort-Object Status, Domain | Export-Csv -Path $OutputPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
Write-Host "Report written to $OutputPath" -ForegroundColor Green

$report | Group-Object Status | Select-Object Name, Count | Format-Table -AutoSize
$report | Group-Object Domain | Sort-Object Count -Descending |
    Select-Object -First 10 Name, Count | Format-Table -AutoSize
```

## Required permissions/roles
- Delegated scopes: User.Read.All and AuditLog.Read.All (admin consent is needed once).
- Signed-in role: Global Reader, Reports Reader or Security Reader is enough for reading; no write role is required.
- signInActivity needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 in the tenant.

## How to adapt
- Remove guests after review: pipe approved ObjectIds into Remove-MgUser -UserId with -WhatIf first, or disable them with Update-MgUser -AccountEnabled:$false.
- Re-send invitations for pending guests with New-MgInvitation -InvitedUserEmailAddress -InviteRedirectUrl (scope User.Invite.All).
- Add a Team or group name column by expanding the memberOf results when you need a per-project view.
- Schedule it monthly in Azure Automation and mail the CSV to the guest sponsor or security team.

## Common mistakes
- Treating an empty last sign-in as proof of inactivity: sign-in data starts when the feature was enabled for the tenant, so combine it with account age.
- Forgetting that guests can hold access through group, Team or SharePoint sharing links, so disabling the account is safer than deleting during review.
- Running with -IncludeGroupCount on tens of thousands of guests without expecting throttling; run it off-hours.
- Reviewing only the UPN: guest UPNs contain #EXT#, so use the Mail column to see the real external address and domain.

title: Find inactive Microsoft 365 user accounts and disable them safely
summary: Report enabled Entra ID accounts with no sign-in for N days, skip break-glass and synced accounts, and optionally disable the rest with WhatIf and Confirm support.
body:
# Find inactive Microsoft 365 user accounts and disable them safely

Inactive but licensed accounts cost money and widen your attack surface. This script finds them using the signInActivity data in Microsoft Entra ID, writes a CSV for review, and can disable the confirmed ones.

## What it does
- Lists enabled accounts (members, optionally guests) with their last interactive, non-interactive and successful sign-in.
- Treats an account as inactive when its newest activity (or, for accounts that never signed in, its creation date) is older than the threshold.
- Counts assigned licenses so you can quantify savings.
- Skips excluded UPNs such as break-glass accounts and flags accounts synced from on-premises AD, which must be disabled there.
- With -DisableAccounts it disables the rest, honoring -WhatIf and -Confirm. The CSV is still written during a -WhatIf run, so you can review the candidates first.

## Script
```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Reports and optionally disables inactive Entra ID accounts.
.EXAMPLE
  .\Get-InactiveUsers.ps1 -InactiveDays 120 -ExcludeUpn 'breakglass1@contoso.com'
  .\Get-InactiveUsers.ps1 -InactiveDays 120 -DisableAccounts -WhatIf
#>
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess, ConfirmImpact = 'High')]
param(
    [ValidateRange(30,3650)][int]$InactiveDays = 90,
    [string[]]$ExcludeUpn = @(),
    [switch]$IncludeGuests,
    [switch]$DisableAccounts,
    [string]$OutputPath = ".\InactiveUsers_$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd').csv"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$scopes = @('User.Read.All','AuditLog.Read.All')
if ($DisableAccounts) { $scopes = @('User.Read.All','User.EnableDisableAccount.All','AuditLog.Read.All') }

try { Connect-MgGraph -Scopes $scopes -NoWelcome }
catch { Write-Error "Graph connection failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return }

$props = 'id','displayName','userPrincipalName','userType','accountEnabled','createdDateTime',
         'assignedLicenses','onPremisesSyncEnabled','signInActivity','department','jobTitle'
$filter = "accountEnabled eq true"
if (-not $IncludeGuests) { $filter += " and userType eq 'Member'" }

try { $users = Get-MgUser -Filter $filter -All -Property $props -PageSize 500 }
catch { Write-Error "User query failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return }

$cutoff = (Get-Date).AddDays(-$InactiveDays)
$rows = foreach ($u in $users) {
    if ($ExcludeUpn -contains $u.UserPrincipalName) { continue }
    $sa = $u.SignInActivity
    $last = @($sa.LastSuccessfulSignInDateTime,$sa.LastSignInDateTime,$sa.LastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime) |
            Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
    $reference = if ($last) { $last } else { $u.CreatedDateTime }
    if ($reference -ge $cutoff) { continue }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        UserPrincipalName = $u.UserPrincipalName
        DisplayName       = $u.DisplayName
        UserType          = $u.UserType
        Department        = $u.Department
        LastActivity      = $last
        NeverSignedIn     = -not $last
        DaysInactive      = [int]((Get-Date) - $reference).TotalDays
        LicenseCount      = @($u.AssignedLicenses).Count
        SyncedFromAD      = [bool]$u.OnPremisesSyncEnabled
        Action            = if ($u.OnPremisesSyncEnabled) { 'Disable in on-prem AD' } else { 'Disable in Entra' }
        ObjectId          = $u.Id
    }
}

# -WhatIf:$false keeps the report writing even during a -WhatIf run (the script's -WhatIf would otherwise be inherited by Export-Csv)
$rows | Sort-Object DaysInactive -Descending | Export-Csv $OutputPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8 -WhatIf:$false
Write-Host ("{0} inactive accounts, {1} licenses assigned. Report: {2}" -f `
    @($rows).Count, ($rows | Measure-Object LicenseCount -Sum).Sum, $OutputPath) -ForegroundColor Cyan

if ($DisableAccounts) {
    foreach ($r in $rows | Where-Object { -not $_.SyncedFromAD }) {
        if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($r.UserPrincipalName, "Disable account (inactive $($r.DaysInactive) days)")) {
            try { Update-MgUser -UserId $r.ObjectId -AccountEnabled:$false -ErrorAction Stop }
            catch { Write-Warning "Failed for $($r.UserPrincipalName): $($_.Exception.Message)" }
        }
    }
}
```

## Required permissions/roles
- Report only: User.Read.All and AuditLog.Read.All; Global Reader or Reports Reader.
- Disabling: User.EnableDisableAccount.All together with User.Read.All (User.ReadWrite.All also works but is broader); the signed-in admin needs User Administrator or higher. Disabling privileged accounts additionally requires Privileged Authentication Administrator or Global Administrator.
- signInActivity requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.

## How to adapt
- Add a license-removal step with Set-MgUserLicense -UserId -AddLicenses @() -RemoveLicenses @(skuId) after a grace period.
- Exclude service accounts by a naming convention or an extension attribute instead of a static list.
- Move disabled users into a review group, wait 30 days, then delete and rely on the recycle bin (30 days) as a safety net.
- Send the CSV to each manager using the Manager property (Get-MgUserManager) before disabling.
- The script uses ConfirmImpact High, so every account prompts. After you reviewed the -WhatIf output, add -Confirm:$false to run unattended.

## Common mistakes
- Disabling shared mailbox, room or service accounts that never sign in interactively. Exclude them first.
- Forgetting break-glass accounts. They are supposed to be inactive.
- Using only LastSignInDateTime: non-interactive sign-ins (mobile mail, token refresh) keep an account in use, so the script takes the newest of all three values.
- Running with -DisableAccounts before reviewing the CSV. Always do a -WhatIf pass first.

title: MFA registration and strength report for all Entra ID users
summary: Uses the authentication methods registration report to list who has no MFA, who relies on weak methods such as SMS, and which admins lack phishing-resistant methods.
body:
# MFA registration and strength report for all Entra ID users

Instead of querying authentication methods user by user (slow and heavily throttled), this script reads the tenant-wide registration report in one paged call and classifies each user by MFA strength.

## What it does
- Pulls userRegistrationDetails for every user with Get-MgReportAuthenticationMethodUserRegistrationDetail.
- Classifies users as NoMFA, WeakMFA (only SMS, voice or email style methods), StandardMFA (authenticator app or OTP) or PhishingResistant (passkey, FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business, certificate).
- Highlights administrators without phishing-resistant methods.
- Exports a CSV and prints a summary table you can paste into a security review.

## Script
```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  MFA registration and method-strength report.
.EXAMPLE
  .\Get-MfaReport.ps1 -AdminsOnly
  .\Get-MfaReport.ps1 -OnlyGaps -OutputPath C:\Temp\mfa-gaps.csv
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$AdminsOnly,
    [switch]$OnlyGaps,
    [string]$OutputPath = ".\MfaReport_$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd').csv"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

try { Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'AuditLog.Read.All' -NoWelcome }
catch { Write-Error "Graph connection failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return }

try {
    $details = Get-MgReportAuthenticationMethodUserRegistrationDetail -All -PageSize 500
}
catch {
    Write-Error "Registration report failed. Check license (Entra ID P1) and role. $($_.Exception.Message)"
    return
}

if ($AdminsOnly) { $details = $details | Where-Object { $_.IsAdmin } }

$phishingResistant = 'fido2|passKey|windowsHelloForBusiness|certificate'
$weakOnly          = '^(mobilePhone|alternateMobilePhone|officePhone|email|securityQuestion)$'

$report = foreach ($d in $details) {
    $methods = @($d.MethodsRegistered)
    $strength =
        if (-not $d.IsMfaRegistered)                                   { 'NoMFA' }
        elseif ($methods -match $phishingResistant)                    { 'PhishingResistant' }
        elseif (@($methods | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch $weakOnly }).Count -eq 0) { 'WeakMFA' }
        else                                                           { 'StandardMFA' }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        UserPrincipalName  = $d.UserPrincipalName
        DisplayName        = $d.UserDisplayName
        UserType           = $d.UserType
        IsAdmin            = $d.IsAdmin
        MfaRegistered      = $d.IsMfaRegistered
        MfaCapable         = $d.IsMfaCapable
        PasswordlessCapable= $d.IsPasswordlessCapable
        SsprRegistered     = $d.IsSsprRegistered
        Strength           = $strength
        Methods            = ($methods -join ';')
        LastUpdated        = $d.LastUpdatedDateTime
    }
}

if ($OnlyGaps) { $report = $report | Where-Object { $_.Strength -in 'NoMFA','WeakMFA' -or ($_.IsAdmin -and $_.Strength -ne 'PhishingResistant') } }

$report | Sort-Object IsAdmin -Descending | Export-Csv $OutputPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
Write-Host "Report written to $OutputPath" -ForegroundColor Green

$report | Group-Object Strength | Select-Object Name, Count | Format-Table -AutoSize
$report | Where-Object { $_.IsAdmin -and $_.Strength -ne 'PhishingResistant' } |
    Select-Object UserPrincipalName, Strength, Methods | Format-Table -AutoSize
```

## Required permissions/roles
- Delegated scope AuditLog.Read.All (admin consent required).
- Signed-in role: Reports Reader, Security Reader, Global Reader, Authentication Administrator or higher.
- The registration report requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 in the tenant.

## How to adapt
- For per-user details (device names, phone numbers masked) call Get-MgUserAuthenticationMethod -UserId and inspect the odata.type of each result; scope UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All.
- Feed the NoMFA list into a group and target it with a Conditional Access policy that requires registration or an authentication strength.
- Schedule weekly and track the NoMFA and WeakMFA counts as a security KPI.
- Filter by department or country using a join against Get-MgUser if you want regional breakdowns.

## Common mistakes
- Reading "MFA registered" as "MFA enforced". The report shows what users registered, not whether a policy requires it. Compare with Conditional Access sign-in results.
- Ignoring guests and service accounts: filter on UserType when the report is for employees only.
- Assuming SMS counts as strong. Treat it as the fallback you are trying to retire.
- Running per-user authentication method calls for 50,000 users instead of the registration report; you will hit throttling.

title: Intune device compliance export with per-policy failure details
summary: Exports all managed devices with compliance state, OS, last sync and encryption, flags stale devices, and lists devices failing each compliance policy using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
body:
# Intune device compliance export with per-policy failure details

Helpdesk and security teams keep asking "which devices are non-compliant and why?" This script produces two CSVs: a device inventory with compliance state, and a policy-level list of every device reporting NonCompliant, Error or Conflict.

## What it does
- Reads all Intune managed devices with Get-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice.
- Filters by operating system and compliance state on the client side (more reliable than combined server filters).
- Flags devices that have not synced for the number of days you choose.
- With -IncludePolicyStatus, loops through every device compliance policy and exports failing device statuses.
- Prints a summary by OS and compliance state.

## Script
```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Exports Intune device compliance data.
.EXAMPLE
  .\Export-IntuneCompliance.ps1 -OperatingSystem Windows -StaleDays 14 -IncludePolicyStatus
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [ValidateSet('All','Windows','iOS','Android','macOS')][string]$OperatingSystem = 'All',
    [switch]$NonCompliantOnly,
    [int]$StaleDays = 30,
    [switch]$IncludePolicyStatus,
    [string]$OutputFolder = '.'
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$scopes = @('DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All')
if ($IncludePolicyStatus) { $scopes += 'DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All' }

try { Connect-MgGraph -Scopes $scopes -NoWelcome }
catch { Write-Error "Graph connection failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return }

$props = 'id','deviceName','userPrincipalName','operatingSystem','osVersion','complianceState',
         'managedDeviceOwnerType','enrolledDateTime','lastSyncDateTime','manufacturer','model',
         'serialNumber','isEncrypted','azureADDeviceId','complianceGracePeriodExpirationDateTime'
try {
    $devices = Get-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice -All -PageSize 500 -Property $props
}
catch { Write-Error "Device query failed: $($_.Exception.Message)"; return }

if ($OperatingSystem -ne 'All') { $devices = $devices | Where-Object { $_.OperatingSystem -eq $OperatingSystem } }
if ($NonCompliantOnly)          { $devices = $devices | Where-Object { $_.ComplianceState -ne 'compliant' } }   # everything except 'compliant': includes noncompliant, inGracePeriod, error, conflict, unknown

$cutoff = (Get-Date).AddDays(-$StaleDays)
$deviceReport = foreach ($d in $devices) {
    [pscustomobject]@{
        DeviceName      = $d.DeviceName
        User            = $d.UserPrincipalName
        OS              = $d.OperatingSystem
        OSVersion       = $d.OsVersion
        Compliance      = $d.ComplianceState
        GraceExpires    = $d.ComplianceGracePeriodExpirationDateTime
        Ownership       = $d.ManagedDeviceOwnerType
        Encrypted       = $d.IsEncrypted
        Manufacturer    = $d.Manufacturer
        Model           = $d.Model
        Serial          = $d.SerialNumber
        Enrolled        = $d.EnrolledDateTime
        LastSync        = $d.LastSyncDateTime
        Stale           = ($d.LastSyncDateTime -lt $cutoff)
        EntraDeviceId   = $d.AzureADDeviceId
    }
}
$stamp = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd'
$devPath = Join-Path $OutputFolder "IntuneDevices_$stamp.csv"
$deviceReport | Export-Csv $devPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
Write-Host "Devices: $(@($deviceReport).Count) -> $devPath" -ForegroundColor Green
$deviceReport | Group-Object OS, Compliance | Select-Object Name, Count | Format-Table -AutoSize

if ($IncludePolicyStatus) {
    $failing = foreach ($p in Get-MgDeviceManagementDeviceCompliancePolicy -All) {
        try {
            $statuses = Get-MgDeviceManagementDeviceCompliancePolicyDeviceStatus -DeviceCompliancePolicyId $p.Id -All -ErrorAction Stop
        }
        catch { Write-Warning "Status failed for policy $($p.DisplayName): $($_.Exception.Message)"; continue }
        foreach ($s in $statuses | Where-Object { $_.Status -in 'nonCompliant','error','conflict' }) {
            [pscustomobject]@{
                Policy = $p.DisplayName; Device = $s.DeviceDisplayName; User = $s.UserPrincipalName
                Status = $s.Status; LastReported = $s.LastReportedDateTime
            }
        }
    }
    $polPath = Join-Path $OutputFolder "IntunePolicyFailures_$stamp.csv"
    $failing | Export-Csv $polPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8
    $failing | Group-Object Policy, Status | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object Name, Count | Format-Table -AutoSize
}
```

## Required permissions/roles
- DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All for devices; DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All for policy status.
- Roles: Intune Administrator, Global Reader, or an Intune custom role with read access to managed devices and compliance policies.

## How to adapt
- Trigger a sync for stale devices with Sync-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice -ManagedDeviceId (needs DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All); use -WhatIf awareness in your wrapper.
- Join with Entra device objects (Get-MgDevice) to find devices registered in Entra but missing in Intune.
- For detailed per-setting failures, query the compliance setting state summaries for a single policy.
- Send the policy failure CSV to the owning team and track the count weekly.

## Common mistakes
- Treating "inGracePeriod" as compliant. Grace periods expire and then Conditional Access blocks the user.
- Ignoring stale devices: a device that has not synced in months still shows its last known (often compliant) state.
- Running without paging on large tenants. Always use -All and a sensible -PageSize.
- Confusing Intune compliance state with Defender risk signals; they are separate inputs unless connected in a policy.
